title: Analysis of Primary Cilia in Rodent Brain By Immunofluorescence Microscopy
author: Shahzad S. Khan
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bnwimfce
materials: Choose multiple brain areas to image – The somatosensory area of the cerebral cortex, pyramidal layer of the hippocampus and the striated area of the caudoputamen next to the lateral ventricle. Image four to five regions within each brain area when investigating primary ciliation in various regions of the brain. For dorso-striatal Cholinergic interneurons: Cells are triple-labeled with Goat anti-CHAT (Millipore Sigma), Chicken anti-NeuN (Millipore Sigma), and DAPI. Primary cilia are detected with Rabbit anti-AC3 antibody (EnCOR). Cholinergic interneurons are rare, and only comprise 1-3% of the striatal cell population. They are also large compared to the surrounding glia and medium spiny neurons. 15-20 Cholinergic interneurons per brain section are typically scored. For dorso-striatal astrocytes: Cells are triple-labeled with Chicken anti-GFAP (EnCOR), Guinea pig anti-S100β (Synaptic Systems), and DAPI. Mouse anti-Arl13b (NeuroMab) is used to label glia primary cilia. Like cholinergic interneurons, GFAP+ astrocytes are also rare in the dorsal striatum (Chai et al., 2017), however, most striatal astrocytes are S100β positive. We typically count 15-20 GFAP+ striatal astrocytes per brain section.

steps.title: Prepare animal and anesthesia
steps.instruction: Soak hair surrounding the ventral thorax of the mouse with 70 % (v/v) ethanol. Anesthetize the mouse with 0.1 mL / 10 g body weight of Euthatal (1/5 dilution of 200 mg/mL stock in PBS). Verify anesthetic depth by toe‑pinch (absence of withdrawal reflex).

steps.title: Expose thoracic cavity
steps.instruction: Make a midline incision through the skin over the proximal abdomen and thorax. Dissect skin to expose underlying muscle, cut the abdomen, puncture the diaphragm, and perform a thoracotomy by making bilateral paramidline incisions through the ribs toward the thoracic inlet to expose the thoracic viscera.

steps.title: Exsanguinate and perfuse
steps.instruction: Make an incision to the right atrium to exsanguinate the mouse. Place a catheter into the left ventricle or aorta, first perfuse with saline then with 4 % (v/v) paraformaldehyde (PFA); perfusion may be performed by gravity or pump.

steps.title: Harvest and fix brain
steps.instruction: Cut the skull with sharp scissors, remove the whole brain, and immediately submerge it in 4 % (v/v) PFA in a 15 mL plastic conical tube. Incubate overnight at 4 °C with gentle agitation.

steps.title: Cryoprotect brain in sucrose
steps.instruction: Transfer the fixed brain to 30 % (w/v) sucrose solution at 4 °C with gentle agitation until the brain settles to the bottom of the tube (approximately 48 h).

steps.title: Wash brains post‑sucrose
steps.instruction: Wash the brain three times with PBS (Wash 1/3, Wash 2/3, Wash 3/3).

steps.title: Embed in O.C.T. and freeze
steps.instruction: Rinse the brain with PBS, submerge it in a 22 × 22 × 20 mm embedding mold containing O.C.T. compound, note rostral and caudal orientation, then place the mold on dry ice to solidify. Store frozen blocks at –80 °C for long‑term storage.

steps.title: Prepare blocks for sectioning
steps.instruction: Remove blocks from –80 °C storage, place them at –20 °C for at least 10 min to soften.

steps.title: Section brain on cryostat
steps.instruction: Set the cryostat to –20 °C, cut sections at 16 µm thickness, either sagittally or coronally depending on region of interest.

steps.title: Mount sections on slides
steps.instruction: Carefully place sections on SuperFrost microscope slides, allow to dry at room temperature for at least 1 h. Slides may be transferred to –80 °C for long‑term storage.

steps.title: Rehydrate and barrier
steps.instruction: Take slides out of –80 °C, place into room‑temperature PBS for rehydration (~15 min). Use a hydrophobic pen (RPI, #19505) to draw a barrier around each section.

steps.title: Remove excess O.C.T. and permeabilize
steps.instruction: Wash the sections three times with ~50 µL PBS (5 min each) to remove excess O.C.T. Then permeabilize with 0.1 % (v/v) Triton X‑100 in PBS for 15 min, keeping permeabilization time consistent across experiments.

steps.title: Post‑permeabilization washes
steps.instruction: Perform three washes with ~50 µL PBS, 5 min each, to remove detergent.

steps.title: Block non‑specific binding
steps.instruction: Incubate sections in PBS containing 1 % (w/v) BSA and 2 % (v/v) fetal bovine serum for 2 h at room temperature (or overnight at 4 °C).

steps.title: Primary antibody incubation
steps.instruction: Prepare dilution buffer (PBS + 1 % BSA + 1 % DMSO). Add 50 µL per section of primary antibody solution and incubate overnight at 4 °C with gentle rocking. Antibodies: rabbit anti‑AC3 (1:10 000) for neuronal cilia, mouse anti‑Arl13b (1:500) for astrocyte cilia, rabbit anti‑SSTR3 (dilution not specified) for cortical/hippocampal cilia.

steps.title: Wash after primary
steps.instruction: Perform three washes with ~50 µL PBS, 5 min each, to remove excess primary antibody.

steps.title: Secondary antibody incubation
steps.instruction: Incubate sections with 50 µL secondary antibody solution for 2 h at room temperature. Use donkey highly cross‑absorbed H + L antibodies (Life Technologies) conjugated to Alexa 488, Alexa 568 or Alexa 647 at 1:1 000 dilution. Optionally add DAPI to the dilution buffer at 0.1 µg/mL.

steps.title: Wash after secondary
steps.instruction: Perform three washes with ~50 µL PBS, 5 min each, to remove excess secondary antibodies.

steps.title: Final rinse and mounting
steps.instruction: Do a quick wash in H₂O to remove residual buffer. Apply 25 µL Mowiol 4‑88 mounting medium containing 2.5 % DABCO onto the stained tissue, place a 22 × 50 mm coverglass, gently tap to remove bubbles, and aspirate excess Mowiol from the coverglass edges.

steps.title: Dry slides
steps.instruction: Allow slides to dry overnight in the dark before image acquisition.

steps.title: Acquire confocal images
steps.instruction: Image sections using a 63× 1.4 NA or 100× 1.4 NA objective on an SP8 laser‑scanning confocal or Yokogawa spinning‑disk confocal equipped with an emCCD 512 × 512 camera. Acquire Z‑stacks with 0.5–0.75 µm sampling (0.75 µm for interneurons, 0.5 µm for astrocytes). Select top and bottom of the Z‑series to capture the entire cell of interest.

steps.title: Manual cilia measurement
steps.instruction: In FIJI, open the Z‑series, create a maximum Z‑projection, set scale using microscope calibration, then use the segmented line tool (shortcut ‘m’) to trace each cilium and record its length in µm.

steps.title: Automated cilia analysis
steps.instruction: Median‑filter the maximum intensity projections, threshold, skeletonize, and count cilia using Analyze Particles. Measure cilia length with the “Longest shortest path” function on the skeletonized mask.

steps.title: Nuclei counting
steps.instruction: Count nuclei in cortex and striatum from DAPI maximum projections by median‑filtering, applying Fill Holes and Watershed, then Analyze Particles. For hippocampal pyramidal layer, count manually using differential pseudo‑coloring of Z‑stacks.

steps.title: Data pooling and statistics
steps.instruction: Pool all measurements from cells within an individual mouse brain (e.g., 15 cells per section × 3 sections = 1 data point per mouse). Increase statistical power by counting more cells or using more mice. Choose statistical test based on group number (Student’s t‑test for two groups, ANOVA for three or more).
